# WBWriter

> Free, open-source live stage whiteboard for macOS. Performers write on a touchscreen, and the audience sees the writing on the LED wall over NDI® or HDMI, with no UI on stage. Made by 4H1M Production (4H1M, z.s.).

- Website: https://wbwriter.app/
- Download (macOS 13+, Apple Silicon and Intel, signed and notarized): https://github.com/4H1Mzs/wbwriter/releases/latest
- Source code: https://github.com/4H1Mzs/wbwriter
- Current version: 1.5.0
- Price: free
- License: MIT (open source)
- Support: simon@4h1m.com
- Made by: [4H1M, z.s.](https://4h1m.com/), a Czech nonprofit audiovisual production

## What it does

WBWriter is a stripped-down, show-safe stage whiteboard inspired by OpenBoard. Everything is set before the show. In live mode the performer gets only a board and an eraser, and the video desk gets a clean signal.

## Features

- **Clean NDI® feed.** Only the inside of the board is sent, with no UI and no border. The NDI source name and frame rate (23.976 to 60 fps) are configurable. Uses NDI 6.3.
- **Black or transparent background.** Black is sent as BGRX. Transparent is sent as BGRA with straight alpha, for keying the writing over graphics.
- **Exact LED wall resolution.** Enter the wall's pixel size (1920×1080, 3840×2160 or custom). The board is scaled to fit the touchscreen with the aspect ratio locked, so what the performer sees is what goes out.
- **HDMI program out.** An optional full-screen clean feed on any external display, alongside NDI or instead of it.
- **Hatched no-draw zone.** The area around the board is hatched, so it's clear where you can't draw. The board stays clear of the MacBook camera notch.
- **Configurable clear button.** A large eraser in the corner you choose. Single tap, double tap (safer), or no button at all.
- **Operator status line.** A small readout beside the board shows NDI health, measured fps, receiver count, network TX, source name, resolution, and battery when running on battery. It never reaches the output.
- **Optional web control.** From a phone on the same network, clear the board or show the performer a message in the hatched area. Messages never reach the outputs. An optional PIN protects it.
- **Built-in updates.** New versions are offered at launch with their changelog and installed only when signed by 4H1M.
- **Show-safe live mode.** Dock and menu bar are hidden and sleep is turned off. Esc goes back to setup.
- **One pen.** White by default, at the thickness of OpenBoard's strongest default pen. Color and width are set before the show.

## Signal chain

Touchscreen (MacBook with a touch display) → WBWriter (renders at the wall's resolution) → NDI® or HDMI → video desk (vMix, OBS, Resolume, TriCaster and others) → LED wall.

## How it works

1. **Set up before the show.** Choose resolution, frame rate, NDI name, background, pen color and width, the clear button's corner and gesture, and which screen is the touchscreen.
2. **Go live.** The board takes over the touchscreen. Receivers see the NDI source as `MACHINE (WBWriter)`.
3. **Write.** Smooth, round strokes at full output resolution.
4. **Clear and repeat.** Tap the eraser between messages. Press Esc when the show is over.

## Platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| macOS 13 or later (Apple Silicon and Intel) | Available |
| Windows | Coming soon |
| Linux | Coming soon |

## Open source

WBWriter is open source under the MIT License. The code, issues, roadmap and releases are public on GitHub: https://github.com/4H1Mzs/wbwriter. It's written in Swift with AppKit. Every tagged version is built, signed and notarized automatically. Bug reports, ideas and pull requests are welcome.

Build from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/4H1Mzs/wbwriter
cd wbwriter
swift run
```

# WBWriter quick start

> How to install WBWriter on macOS, set it up for a show, and send the board to an LED wall over NDI® or HDMI.

## Install

1. Download the latest `.dmg` from https://github.com/4H1Mzs/wbwriter/releases/latest.
2. Open it and drag **WBWriter** into **Applications**.
3. Open WBWriter. When macOS asks to let it find devices on your local network, click **Allow**. NDI can't work without this.

Requirements: macOS 13 or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel.

## Set up the show

All settings are in the setup window and are saved between launches.

![The WBWriter setup window with output, NDI, pen and board settings](https://wbwriter.app/img/setup-window-a9afe185.webp)

| Setting | What to choose |
|---|---|
| Resolution | Your LED wall's pixel size. Presets: 1920×1080, 3840×2160, 2560×1440, 1280×720, 1080×1920 (portrait), or custom. |
| Frame rate | 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Match your video system. |
| Background | *Black* for a normal feed. *Transparent* for an alpha overlay (BGRA, straight alpha). |
| Send NDI® | On or off. |
| NDI source name | Receivers see `MACHINE-NAME (your name)`. |
| Send | *Every frame*, or *Only when the board changes* (then one frame per second while idle). |
| Max frame rate while writing | Same as output, 30, 25, 15 or 10 fps. |
| Resolution over NDI | 100, 75, 50 or 33 % of the output resolution. The receiver scales it back up. |
| Pen color | White by default. |
| Pen width | Pixels at 1080p, scaled with the output resolution. Default 8 matches OpenBoard's thickest default pen. |
| Board display | Which screen is the touchscreen. |
| Margin | Space around the board on the touchscreen. |
| Clear gesture | Single tap, double tap (safer), or none (no button). |
| Clear button | Which corner of the touchscreen it sits in. |
| Corner logo | A small, faint logo in the bottom-right corner of the touchscreen: 4H1M, your own image, or none. It's never sent to the outputs. |
| Hide mouse cursor | Hides the pointer while live. |
| HDMI output | An external display for a clean full-screen feed, or *None*. |
| Web control | Off by default. When on, it shows the address to open on a phone, with an optional port and PIN. |

## Go live

Click **Go Live** or press Return. The board fills the touchscreen, and the Dock and menu bar are hidden.

![Live mode on the touchscreen: the black board with a faint border, the clear button in the corner and the status line below](https://wbwriter.app/img/board-live-3bd3d179.webp)

- Write with a finger, pen or mouse.
- Tap the clear button to erase the board. **Backspace** on a keyboard also clears it.
- Press **Esc** to return to setup.

## Read the status line

A small status line sits outside the board, near the bottom of the touchscreen. When there isn't room below the board, it moves into the margin beside it and wraps onto several lines. It's never sent to NDI or HDMI.

![The status line: NDI state, source name, resolution and frame rate, receivers, network traffic and battery](https://wbwriter.app/img/status-line-60ecde80.webp)

| Indicator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Green `NDI OK` | Sending at the target frame rate, with at least one receiver connected. |
| Yellow `NDI waiting` | Sending fine, but no receiver is connected yet. |
| Red `NDI DROPPING` | Sending below 90% of the target frame rate. |
| `… fps` | Measured send rate. |
| `… rx` | Number of connected NDI receivers. |
| `TX … Mb/s` | Total outgoing traffic on the Mac's Ethernet and Wi-Fi interfaces. |
| `Battery …%` | Shown only on battery power. Turns red at 20% or below. |

## Control it from a phone

Turn on **Web control** in the setup window and open one of the addresses it shows (for example `http://Stage-Mac.local:8080`) on a phone or laptop on the same network.

- **Clear board:** tap twice to confirm.
- **Message to the performer:** shown in yellow in the hatched area of the touchscreen, never on NDI or HDMI. It stays until you tap **Remove message**, or disappears after 10 seconds, 30 seconds or a minute.

- **Uptime:** how long WBWriter has been running and how long it has been live, with the current NDI status and network load.
- **Refresh display:** rebuilds the touchscreen and HDMI windows if a display shows the board wrongly. The writing, the message and NDI keep running.
- **Restart WBWriter:** tap twice. The app restarts and comes back live with the same board and message.

![The WBWriter Remote page on a phone, with Clear board, a message field and Remove message](https://wbwriter.app/img/web-control-3ca9986a.webp)

![A message for the performer shown in yellow below the board on the touchscreen](https://wbwriter.app/img/board-message-226d19b7.webp)

The actions work only while WBWriter is live. Set a PIN if other people share the network. If the macOS firewall is on, allow incoming connections for WBWriter when asked.

## Save network bandwidth (Wi-Fi)

NDI re-sends the whole picture every frame, and a board full of writing costs far more than a black one. A large board at a high frame rate can need well over 100 Mb/s, which Wi-Fi often can't sustain. To lower it:

- Set **Send** to *Only when the board changes*. After the performer stops writing, traffic drops to almost nothing, even with the writing still on the board.
- Lower **Max frame rate while writing** to 25 or 15 fps. Writing stays readable, with slightly more latency.
- Lower **Resolution over NDI**. 50 % needs about a quarter of the bandwidth. White strokes on black only soften slightly.

The setup window estimates the saving, and **TX** in the status line shows the real network load. Ethernet is still the most reliable option for big boards.

## Receive the feed

Any NDI receiver works, for example vMix, OBS with DistroAV, Resolume, NDI Studio Monitor, TriCaster or disguise. Look for the source named `MACHINE (WBWriter)`, or whatever name you set.

## Test without touching the screen

Run `/Applications/WBWriter.app/Contents/MacOS/WBWriter --selftest`. WBWriter goes live right away and draws a test stroke, which is useful for checking NDI or HDMI routing from the video desk.

Support: simon@4h1m.com

NDI® is a registered trademark of Vizrt NDI AB. Learn more at https://ndi.video/.

# WBWriter FAQ and troubleshooting

> Answers to common questions about WBWriter, the free, open-source stage whiteboard for macOS with NDI® and HDMI output.

## Is WBWriter free?

Yes. WBWriter is free and open source under the MIT License. It's made by 4H1M, z.s., a Czech nonprofit. If it helps your show, you can support 4H1M at https://www.darujme.cz/4h1m.

## Which platforms are supported?

macOS 13 or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel. Windows and Linux builds are coming soon.

## The NDI source doesn't appear on my receiver.

- Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network** and make sure WBWriter is turned on.
- Check that the Mac and the receiver are on the same network and subnet.
- Check that multicast and mDNS (Bonjour) aren't blocked by the network switch or firewall.
- Look at the status line on the touchscreen. `NDI waiting` means WBWriter is sending and no receiver has connected yet.

## The NDI feed drops out over Wi-Fi.

A big board at a high frame rate can use more than 100 Mb/s while there's writing on it. In the setup window, set **Send** to *Only when the board changes*, lower **Max frame rate while writing**, and lower **Resolution over NDI**. The quick start explains each option. Ethernet is the most reliable fix.

## Can I key the writing over other graphics?

Yes. Set **Background** to *Transparent*. WBWriter then sends BGRA with straight alpha, so the receiver can key out everything except the writing.

## What does the performer see compared with the audience?

The board on the touchscreen has exactly the aspect ratio of the output. Everything inside the board is sent pixel for pixel. The hatched area, border, clear button and status line stay on the touchscreen only.

![The touchscreen in live mode. Only the inside of the board is sent to the LED wall.](https://wbwriter.app/img/board-live-3bd3d179.webp)

## Can I prevent someone from clearing the board by accident?

Set **Clear gesture** to *Double tap*, or to *None* to hide the button entirely. An operator can still clear the board with Backspace on a keyboard.

## Can I change the pen during the show?

No. Pen color and width are set in the setup window before the show, so nothing can change by accident in live mode.

## The touchscreen shows the board wrongly, or WBWriter misbehaves.

With **Web control** turned on, open the remote page on a phone. **Refresh display** rebuilds the touchscreen and HDMI windows without interrupting NDI or losing the writing. If that doesn't help, **Restart WBWriter** (tap twice): the app restarts and returns live with the same board and message.

## How do I update WBWriter?

WBWriter checks for a new version each time it starts and shows the changelog when one is available. Click **Install and Restart**: it downloads the update, checks that it's signed by 4H1M, replaces the app and opens it again. You can also choose **WBWriter → Check for Updates…** at any time, or turn off the automatic check under **Updates** in the setup window. The check never interrupts live mode.

## How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?

Open an issue at https://github.com/4H1Mzs/wbwriter/issues, or email simon@4h1m.com.

NDI® is a registered trademark of Vizrt NDI AB. Learn more at https://ndi.video/.
